title: The challenge of merging project management and agile terms
blurb: Explain why merging project management and agile is hard, how PRINCE2 Agile handles it, and pair each PRINCE2 term with its agile counterpart.
question: A project board member asks why the PRINCE2 Agile book talks about both 'stage plans' and 'release maps'. What is the challenge behind this, and how does the book deal with it?

teach.body: Merging project management and agile is challenging because the two have no common ground in terminology. Project management speaks of business cases, stages, tolerances and reports; agile speaks of backlogs, user stories, iterations and stand-ups. To bridge the gap, the PRINCE2 Agile book uses a combination of project management terms and agile terms, so both communities can recognise what is meant.

teach.h: Combine, do not replace the purpose
teach.body: A mixed term keeps the PRINCE2 purpose while taking an agile form. A release map still does the job of a project or stage plan; a team dashboard still tells the project manager how the work is going, as a checkpoint report did. That is why PRINCE2 Agile can keep governance and control throughout while teams work in an agile way.

teach.note: PRINCE2 Agile uses generic words such as 'iteration' so it is not tied to one framework.

teach.h: Worked scenario: Linden Vale Housing Association
teach.body: Linden Vale Housing Association is building a tenant repairs portal. Its developers have worked with Scrum; its board knows PRINCE2. Project manager Grace Okafor finds the board asking for 'highlight reports' while the team talks of 'sprint reviews'. She agrees a one-page glossary: the project dashboard does the job of the highlight report, iterations are the team's sprints, and each work package is a set of user stories agreed with the product owner. Both groups now mean the same thing.

teach.text: The merging challenge is about TERMINOLOGY: the two worlds have no common ground in their terms. It is not that agile and PRINCE2 cannot work together, and it is not solved by choosing one vocabulary and banning the other. The book uses a combination of both.

items: Project management and agile have no common ground in terminology (5.8).
The PRINCE2 Agile book uses a combination of both sets of terms.
Business case pairs with project canvas; project and stage plans with the release map.
Product description pairs with product backlog; work package description with a set of user stories.
Checkpoint report pairs with team dashboard; highlight report with project dashboard.
A mixed term keeps the PRINCE2 purpose while taking an agile form.

summary: You can now explain the challenge of merging project management and agile and how the book handles it. You can also pair the main PRINCE2 terms with their agile counterparts.

A.q: Why can merging project management and agile prove challenging?
options: The two approaches use different tolerance levels
The two have no common ground in terminology
Agile does not allow any project governance
A.why: Book 5.8: the challenge is that the two have no common ground in terminology.

whyNot.0: Tolerances are part of PRINCE2 governance; the stated challenge is the lack of shared terms.
whyNot.2: PRINCE2 Agile keeps governance and control throughout an agile project.
whyNot.3: PRINCE2 Project Management can host iterative delivery; PRINCE2 Agile is built for it.

A.q: How does the PRINCE2 Agile book deal with the challenge of merging project management and agile?
options: It replaces agile terms with PRINCE2 terms
It replaces PRINCE2 terms with Scrum terms
It uses a combination of both sets of terms
It defines a third, new set of terms
A.why: To mediate the challenge, the book uses a combination of project management and agile terms (5.8).

whyNot.0: The book keeps agile terms such as backlog, iteration and user story.
whyNot.1: The book keeps PRINCE2 terms and uses generic agile words rather than one framework's terms.
whyNot.3: It combines existing terms from both worlds rather than inventing a separate vocabulary.

A.q: In PRINCE2 Agile, which agile artifact is used in place of the checkpoint report?
A.why: The team dashboard replaces the checkpoint report; the PM pulls information from it (Table 12.1).

whyNot.0: The project dashboard replaces the highlight report and end stage report.
whyNot.1: The release map serves as the project plan and stage plan.
whyNot.2: The product backlog takes the place of product descriptions.

B.q: Which pairing of a PRINCE2 management product and its agile counterpart is correct?
B.why: The business case is tailored to the project canvas in PRINCE2 Agile (6.3.2, Table 5.2).

whyNot.0: The project plan pairs with the release map; the team dashboard replaces the checkpoint report.
whyNot.2: The highlight report pairs with the project dashboard.
whyNot.3: Product descriptions pair with the product backlog.

B.q: Identify the missing words in the following sentence. In PRINCE2 Agile, a work package description is typically expressed as a [?].
B.why: A work package description is commonly a set of user stories agreed between the project manager and the product owner.

whyNot.1: The project product description is replaced by the project backlog; it does not describe a work package.
whyNot.2: The release map is the agile form of the project and stage plans.
whyNot.3: The team dashboard is the agile form of the checkpoint report.

B.q:
Which two statements about merging project management and agile are correct?
1. The two have no common ground in terminology.
2. PRINCE2 Agile drops the business case in favour of a backlog.
3. The book uses a combination of project management and agile terms.
4. Agile terms are used for governance and PRINCE2 terms for delivery.
B.why: Book 5.8: the two have no common ground in terminology, so a combination of both sets of terms is used.

whyNot.0: Statement 2 is wrong: the business case is tailored to a project canvas, not dropped.
whyNot.1: Both are wrong: the business case stays, and there is no such split of vocabularies.
whyNot.2: Statement 4 is wrong: the terms are combined, not divided between governance and delivery.

C.q: A board used to PRINCE2 asks for highlight reports, while the delivery team keeps its team dashboards. Which artifact should the project manager use to give the board equivalent information?
options: The project canvas, refreshed after each iteration
The team dashboards, forwarded by email to the board
The project dashboard, which the board pulls from
The release map, presented at each team stand-up
C.why: The project dashboard replaces the highlight report; it is updated and reviewed in progress review workshops and the board pulls information from it (Table 12.1).

whyNot.0: The project canvas is the business justification, not the regular status report.
whyNot.1: Team dashboards replace checkpoint reports, which serve the project manager, not the board.
whyNot.3: The release map is the plan; the board's regular status comes from the project dashboard.

C.q: Which statement BEST describes how a mixed term such as 'release map' works in PRINCE2 Agile?
options: It keeps the purpose of the plan and gives it an agile form
It removes the need for any plan at stage level
It is used by teams, while the board keeps a Gantt chart
It replaces the business case for the whole project
C.why: The release map serves as the project plan and stage plan: the PRINCE2 purpose is kept, the form is agile (8.3.2.5).

whyNot.1: The release map is the stage-level plan; stage planning still happens.
whyNot.2: The release map serves as the project and stage plan for the board too.
whyNot.3: The business case is tailored to the project canvas, not the release map.

C.q: A developer from a Scrum background asks which PRINCE2 Agile term covers the 'sprint' her team runs. Which term should the project manager give her?
C.why: PRINCE2 Agile uses the generic word 'iteration' for a timeboxed cycle such as a Scrum sprint; iterations sit inside releases and stages.

whyNot.0: A stage is the highest timebox level and normally contains several releases and iterations.
whyNot.1: A release usually contains two to four iterations.
whyNot.3: A work package is the set of work authorized for a team, often a set of user stories.

reteach.title: Two languages, one meeting
reteach.question: How would you run a meeting where half the room speaks one language and half speaks another?

blocks.body: You would not ban either language. You would agree a phrasebook so each important idea has a word both sides recognise. PRINCE2 Agile does the same: board members keep 'business case' and 'stage', teams keep 'backlog' and 'iteration', and the book pairs them so a project canvas is understood as the business case and a release map as the plan.

blocks.text: The problem is the words, not the ideas: no common ground in terminology. The fix is to combine the terms, not to pick a winner.

explain.body: Project management and agile have no common ground in terminology, which makes merging them challenging (5.8).

test.q: According to PRINCE2 Agile, what makes merging project management and agile challenging?
test.why: The two have no common ground in terminology (5.8).

whyNot.0: Contracts are handled in the commercial management approach; they are not the stated challenge.
whyNot.1: Team size relates to scaling, not to the merging challenge.
whyNot.3: PRINCE2 Agile applies the seven principles; the stated challenge is terminology.

explain.body: To mediate the challenge, the PRINCE2 Agile book uses a combination of project management and agile terms.

test.q: What approach does the PRINCE2 Agile book take to terminology?
options: It combines project management and agile terms
It uses Scrum terms throughout the method
It keeps PRINCE2 terms and drops agile terms
It invents new terms for every product
test.why: A combination of project management and agile terms is used in the book (5.8).

whyNot.1: PRINCE2 Agile uses generic agile words, not one framework's terms.
whyNot.2: Agile terms such as backlog and iteration are kept.
whyNot.3: Existing terms from both worlds are combined.

explain.body: Project and stage plans pair with the release map. The project product description pairs with the project backlog, and product descriptions with product backlogs.

test.q: Which agile artifact serves as the project plan and stage plan in PRINCE2 Agile?
test.why: The release map serves as the project plan and stage plan (8.3.2.5).

whyNot.0: The project backlog replaces the project product description.
whyNot.1: The project canvas is the business case form.
whyNot.2: The team dashboard replaces the checkpoint report.

explain.body: The checkpoint report pairs with the team dashboard, the highlight report with the project dashboard, and the team manager with the product owner.

test.q: Which agile counterpart is paired with the PRINCE2 highlight report?
test.why: The project dashboard replaces the highlight report (and the end stage report) (Table 12.1).

whyNot.0: The team dashboard replaces the checkpoint report.
whyNot.2: A burn chart may appear on a dashboard but is not the counterpart of the report.
whyNot.3: The end project report is kept in PRINCE2 Agile for closure; it is not the regular status report.
